ledger.claim: Under POL-RD-01 the trace distance governs, and it puts this trip at 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km: an excess of 2.98 km, which is 36.34% of optimal. Both establishment limbs are cleared — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms — so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The rounded 11.2 km on trip_record.actual_distance_km is a convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test.

The rider carries and discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00103 with a consistent start, and the excess is measured from a wholly unimpaired trace — 100% coverage, a 10 second sampling interval and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so no limb of POL-RD-07 is engaged and no independent corroboration is required. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the extra-corroboration rider for sub-30% claims does not apply.

The rider does not contest the distance and time charges. The LTA advisory for the Braddell Road closure (ADV-20260714-031) satisfies POL-RD-03 on every limb — it names the arterial the optimal route uses, its 05:30–12:00 window covers the trip window, and the trace leaves the corridor at the Lorong 1 Toa Payoh slip and rejoins it after — so the justified excess is the lesser of 2.98 km and 1.30 × (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.0 = 4.12 km, namely 2.98 km, and the whole measured excess is exonerated. That exoneration reaches the distance and time lines only. Government-set and third-party pass-throughs are settled separately under POL-RD-09, and it is there the rider's case lies.

The off-route ERP must come back to the rider. The fare breakdown charges $4.00 of ERP, both lines on the CTE — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00 — each recorded on_optimal_route false, while the trip record puts optimal_route_erp_sgd at $0.00 because the optimal arterial route crosses no gantry at all. These are genuine crossings, not phantom lines: the nearest trace fix is 0.0 m from the first gantry and 40.2 m from the second, both inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 uses. They are real charges incurred on a corridor the optimal route never touches. Where a deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) still refunds the off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction. The rider neither chose the CTE nor caused the closure, and $4.00 sits well under the $12.00 cap.

Nothing in the chat log bars that refund. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only on a rider instruction that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on, and the only instruction here — 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' — came from the driver, not the rider. The rider's one-word 'ok' is bare acknowledgement of a closure the driver had already announced; it names no place and no route. Both messages carry waypoint_hint null, so there is no rider waypoint for the trace to corroborate. POL-RD-09(3)'s bar on ERP refunds for rider-caused detours is therefore not engaged, and the POL-RD-09(2) pass-through correction stands.

If the tribunal instead runs POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route that POL-RD-03 directs — 8.2 km + 2.98 km = 11.18 km, 28.6 minutes — the recomputed fare is $20.99 against a charged total of $25.12, a refund of $4.13 rounding up to $4.15. POL-RD-09(1) requires that figure to comprehend the off-route ERP rather than have the $4.00 added on top of it, so the rider seeks the larger of the two routes to the same entitlement, not both together.

The measured excess on this trip is fully exonerated by a road closure, under POL-RD-03 limb (a). The LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 names 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' - and the platform's own optimal route for this booking is recorded as 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry', so the advisory names the very road the optimal route traverses.

POL-RD-03 limb (b) is satisfied on the timestamps. The advisory was valid from 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026 and overlaps the trip window (first fix 08:07:20, last fix 08:36:20) by 35.2 minutes - far more than the 15-minute buffer the clause allows at each end. Both the window and the geometry are recorded as checking out against the trace.

POL-RD-03 limb (c) is satisfied: the trace shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor and rejoining it after the affected segment. The fare record itemises two charged gantries, both flagged on_optimal_route = false, and the trace passes within 0.0 m and 40.25 m of them at 08:12:50 and 08:19:40 respectively - i.e. the vehicle actually travelled the diversion corridor the advisory describes.

The exoneration cap covers the whole of the measured excess. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km. The cap is 4.12 km and the measured excess is 2.98 km, so nothing is left unexonerated.

Applied to the route, the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km - which is exactly the trace distance of 11.18 km on the same record. The excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment is therefore zero, and a deviation measured against the adjusted optimal route does not survive.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 does not run against the booked optimal route and no distance-or-time refund is owed on those lines. The driver was directed off Braddell Road by a HIGH-severity, all-lanes closure with an LTA diversion instruction; the distance and time charges stand because he is not at fault.

Even on the platform's own closure-adjusted recomputation - the reading most favourable to the rider - the arithmetic cannot reach the SGD 9.00 claimed. charged_total is 25.12 and the closure-adjusted recomputed_fare is 20.993, a difference of 4.127, which rounds up to SGD 4.15 payable. The rider's claim is roughly double any figure the route-deviation arithmetic on this record produces.

The entire residual is the off-route ERP pass-through. The optimal route carries ERP of SGD 0.00 while the charged lines total SGD 4.00, of which SGD 4.00 is flagged off-optimal-route. Under POL-RD-09(1) that ERP is already comprehended in any POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added on top of it, and under POL-RD-09(2) it is at most a standalone pass-through correction capped at SGD 12.00 - it is a government charge the driver never keeps, so it cannot support a refund of distance or time charges.

This is not a billing-integrity case under POL-RD-09(4). Both charged gantries are matched to the trace by the clause's own test: the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry has a nearest fix at 0.0 m and the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry at 40.25 m, both well inside the 250 m match radius. There is no phantom line and no gantry the trace never passes, so no full standalone refund of the ERP on that ground is available.

The rider himself approved the expressway routing, and under POL-RD-09(3) no ERP refund is due where the detour is rider-caused. The chat log records the driver announcing the Braddell closure and stating 'i take CTE ah' at 08:12:30, and the rider replying 'ok' at 08:12:58 - before the first gantry was charged at 08:14:06 and within the 3-minute window of the corridor exit that POL-RD-04(b) allows. The road was named in the thread and the trace independently corroborates that the vehicle travelled it (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.25 m from the two CTE gantries), which is the corroboration POL-RD-04 requires.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to escalate this into a full refund or a conduct referral. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed trips in 90 days, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test (3 or more flags; or a ratio of 0.05 or more) is met, and the deviation here is in any event not MATERIAL: 36.34% is below the 50% materiality figure and 2.98 km is below the 8.0 km figure.

The burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged by the driver on this record: he points to a specific artifact (the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01, which carries an advisory_id, a validity window and route geometry all matching this trip) and a specific clause (POL-RD-03), and the trace independently corroborates the diversion it describes. That is the article-and-clause answer POL-RD-08 demands, not a general assertion that traffic was bad.

On the record as a whole the rider's own claim is confined to the ERP ('Please refund at least the ERP'), and the evidence gives him nothing on the distance and time lines because the closure exonerates them in full. To the extent any amount moves at all it is the SGD 4.00 off-route ERP pass-through and no more - a correction against a government charge, not a finding against this driver's routing.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, on trip TRP-00103 (Bishan to Kallang Wave Mall, 14 July 2026).

The diversion is established and fully excused. The GPS trace records 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34% — which clears POL-RD-01's establishment tests, and the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 10-second fixes, no gaps, so no POL-RD-07 limb fires). The LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 (Braddell Road towards Serangoon, all lanes closed 05:30–12:00) satisfies every limb of POL-RD-03: it names the arterial the optimal route uses, its window covers the trip by 35.2 minutes, and the trace leaves and rejoins that corridor. The justified excess is min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12) = 2.98 km, which is the whole measured excess, so the deviation is exonerated in full. Because an exculpatory clause fully excuses it, POL-RD-02 does not run and the distance and time charges stand — no refund arises on those lines.

The ERP is refunded separately. The fare breakdown charges $4.00 of ERP — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00 — each itemised as not on the optimal route, while the optimal arterial route crosses no gantry (optimal-route ERP $0.00). Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) refunds the off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. The two gantries are genuine crossings — the trace passes within 0.0 m and 40.25 m of them, inside the 250 m match radius — so this is not a phantom-line billing defect under POL-RD-09(4). The refund is $4.00, rounded to $4.00.

The chat does not convert this into a rider-caused detour. The driver wrote 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' at 08:12:30 and the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58. I have not treated this as a rider instruction under POL-RD-04, and have rejected the driver's claim that POL-RD-09(3) bars the ERP refund: the instruction came from the driver, the rider named no place or road, and both messages carry waypoint_hint null, so there is no rider waypoint for the trace to corroborate. POL-RD-09(3) is therefore not engaged and the ERP correction stands. I have also not adopted the rider's alternative figure of $4.15 from a POL-RD-02 recomputation against the closure-adjusted route: POL-RD-03 exonerates the entire excess here, so POL-RD-02 has no unexonerated excess to refund, and the entitlement is the $4.00 standalone ERP correction, not $4.15.

On the driver's conduct: the deviation is not material (36.34% is below 50% and 2.98 km is below 8.0 km), and the driver profile shows 0 deviation flags in the last 90 days against 553 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 does not fire and no conduct referral is made. No driver compensation is due — the billed distance of 11.2 km is not less than the trace's 11.18 km.

Outcome: a partial refund of $4.00 to the rider (charged_total $25.12; off-route ERP $3.00 + $1.00 = $4.00 against optimal-route ERP $0.00, under the $12.00 cap). The remaining distance and time charges stand. Confidence 0.90, resting on artifacts all at weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
